title: Opportunistic infections
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's infection (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for lung infection.

HPI: 90-year-old male pt presents for f/u of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Pt has been on long-term high-dose steroids for a chronic lung condition. Currently undergoing treatment with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Pt reports feeling "much better" since starting meds. Denies increased shortness of breath, productive cough, or chest pain. Reports improved exercise tolerance. No fevers or chills.

Medication List:
- Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (high dose)
- Prednisone (high dose)
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or fatigue.
Respiratory: Denies cough or dyspnea.
Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations.
GI: No nausea or diarrhea.
MSK: No joint pain.

Social History: Retired. Lives at home with spouse. No tobacco use. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had arthritis.

Vitals:
BP: 128/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 95% on RA
Ht/Wt: 5'9", 165 lbs

Recent Labs:
WBC: 7.2
Hgb: 13.8
Plt: 210
Creatinine: 1.1 (eGFR 65)

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears well-nourished and in no acute distress.
Respiratory: CTAB. Breath sounds clear to auscultation bilaterally. No wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.
Cardiovascular: RRR, S1, S2 regular. No murmurs.
Extremities: No edema.

Assessment:
1. Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia - pt responding well to trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.
2. Chronic lung condition - stable on high-dose steroids.

Plan:
- Continue trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole as prescribed.
- Continue high-dose steroids for lung condition.
- Monitor for any return of respiratory symptoms.
- F/u in 4 weeks for repeat labs and clinical evaluation.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, DO, 05/14/2026

distractors.why: The organism (Pneumocystis) is documented and has its own code.
